guidedExample.explanation: Translated notices must be archived. Other notices may also be archived, so the fact settles neither translation nor its absence.

commonMistake.mistake: Calling an allowed case a proven case.
commonMistake.repair: Ask whether every situation fitting the information includes the conclusion. If both outcomes fit, say unknown.

beginner.prompt: Every tested battery has a sticker. Battery P was tested. What follows?
options: P is the only tested battery.
beginner.hint: Apply the rule to P without adding a reverse rule.
reasoningSteps: P meets the tested condition.
The sticker follows for P alone.
beginner.explanation: P meets the tested condition. The sticker follows for P alone.

beginner.prompt: Every polished lens is clear. Lens J is not clear. What follows?
beginner.hint: Could a polished lens lack the required clarity?
reasoningSteps: Polishing would require clarity.
J lacks clarity, so J cannot be polished under the rule.
beginner.explanation: Polishing would require clarity. J lacks clarity, so J cannot be polished under the rule.

beginner.prompt: Every reserved seat has a marker. Seat W is not reserved. Its marker status is:
beginner.hint: The rule speaks only about reserved seats.
reasoningSteps: An unreserved seat does not activate the rule.
A marker may be present or absent without breaking it.
beginner.explanation: An unreserved seat does not activate the rule. A marker may be present or absent without breaking it.

medium.prompt: Every encrypted file is restricted. Every restricted file is logged. No case fact is supplied. Which follows?
medium.hint: Match the shared restricted condition.
reasoningSteps: Encryption leads to restriction, which leads to logging.
The resulting rule does not assert a file exists.
medium.explanation: Encryption leads to restriction, which leads to logging. The resulting rule does not assert a file exists.

medium.prompt: Every approved replacement part is stocked. Part D is a replacement part, but approval is unknown. What follows?
medium.hint: Replacement part and approved replacement part differ.
reasoningSteps: The trigger includes approval.
The supplied fact does not meet that entire trigger.
medium.explanation: The trigger includes approval. The supplied fact does not meet that entire trigger.

medium.prompt: Every public hearing is recorded. Hearing N is recorded. A student concludes it is public. Which repair is accurate?
options: The rule has no starting condition.
medium.hint: Identify the direction the student added.
reasoningSteps: The rule runs from public status to recording.
The student used its unsupported reverse.
medium.explanation: The rule runs from public status to recording. The student used its unsupported reverse.

advanced.prompt: Every eligible applicant may appeal. Tavi is an eligible applicant. Which follows?
advanced.hint: Preserve the modal word may.
reasoningSteps: Tavi satisfies the complete eligible-applicant condition, which grants appeal permission.
Permission establishes neither action nor acceptance.
advanced.explanation: Tavi satisfies the complete eligible-applicant condition, which grants appeal permission. Permission establishes neither action nor acceptance.

advanced.prompt: Every licensed guide must carry a radio. Guide Z carries no radio. What follows about compliance?
options: Z cannot be licensed in real life.
If Z is licensed, Z violates the stated requirement.
Z must be unlicensed in real life.
advanced.hint: A requirement can be violated; it is not a physical impossibility.
reasoningSteps: A licensed Z would be required to carry a radio.
The fact would show noncompliance, rather than proving absence of a license.
advanced.explanation: A licensed Z would be required to carry a radio. The fact would show noncompliance, rather than proving absence of a license.

advanced.prompt: Every shortlisted design is displayed. Every displayed design is catalogued. Design E is not catalogued. What follows?
advanced.hint: Trace what shortlisting would force for E.
reasoningSteps: Shortlisting would lead through display to cataloguing.
E lacks the final required result, so E is not shortlisted.
advanced.explanation: Shortlisting would lead through display to cataloguing. E lacks the final required result, so E is not shortlisted.

title: Does the Conclusion Have to Follow?
goal: Test whether true premises could coexist with a false conclusion.
teaching: Truth concerns whether a statement matches the facts. Validity concerns the connection between premises and conclusion. To test a deduction, temporarily accept its premises. Ask whether its conclusion could still be false.

Every copper key is magnetic. This key is copper. Therefore this key is magnetic. The reasoning follows the given rule, even if the first premise is false outside the exercise. We are testing the inference, not endorsing the premise.

A counterexample keeps every premise true while making the conclusion false. For A → B and B, therefore A, a case with B but no A does that. Invalid does not mean the conclusion must be false. It means the premises do not establish it.
method: Accept the supplied premises for the inference test.
Identify the exact conclusion.
Try to keep all premises true while making that conclusion false.
If such a case is possible, the conclusion is not guaranteed.

statements: Every circular tile is blue.
Tile P is blue.
Claim: Tile P is circular.
reasoning: The rule allows a blue square tile.
That case preserves the premises and defeats the claim.
workedExample.conclusion: Circularity is not guaranteed.

guidedExample.prompt: Every enrolled swimmer has a locker. Ren is enrolled as a swimmer. Therefore Ren has a locker. The inference is:
options: Invalid because lockers may be expensive.
Invalid because enrollment is not necessary for a locker.
guidedExample.hint: Only test the direction actually used.
reasoningSteps: Ren meets the rule's sufficient condition.
The conclusion is the required result, so it follows.
guidedExample.explanation: Ren meets the rule's sufficient condition. The conclusion is the required result, so it follows.

commonMistake.mistake: Rejecting an inference because a premise sounds unrealistic.
commonMistake.repair: First assess whether the conclusion follows if the premises are true. Assess premise truth as a separate question.

beginner.prompt: Every gold leaf is transparent. Leaf R is gold. Therefore R is transparent. Does the conclusion follow from these premises?
options: No, because gold is not normally transparent.
Only if transparent leaves are gold.
beginner.hint: Treat the unusual premise as given.
reasoningSteps: R satisfies the gold condition.
Transparency follows by the stated rule regardless of real-world plausibility.
beginner.explanation: R satisfies the gold condition. Transparency follows by the stated rule regardless of real-world plausibility.

beginner.prompt: Every bound booklet has a cover. Booklet D has a cover. Therefore D is bound. The problem is:
options: The rule was reversed without support.
beginner.hint: A cover may have another source.
reasoningSteps: The premises allow an unbound covered booklet.
They therefore do not guarantee binding.
beginner.explanation: The premises allow an unbound covered booklet. They therefore do not guarantee binding.

beginner.prompt: An invalid argument's conclusion must be:
options: Neither; validity alone does not settle its truth.
beginner.hint: Failure of proof is not proof of falsity.
reasoningSteps: Invalidity means the premises do not force the conclusion.
The conclusion may still be true for other reasons.
beginner.explanation: Invalidity means the premises do not force the conclusion. The conclusion may still be true for other reasons.

medium.prompt: Every laminated card resists water. Card B resists water. Claim: B is laminated. Which counterexample works?
options: B is laminated and resists water.
B is not laminated and resists water.
B is laminated and does not resist water.
medium.hint: Keep the rule and the resistance fact true.
reasoningSteps: An unlaminated resistant card is permitted by the rule.
It makes the proposed conclusion false while preserving both premises.
medium.explanation: An unlaminated resistant card is permitted by the rule. It makes the proposed conclusion false while preserving both premises.

medium.prompt: Every active beacon transmits. Beacon H does not transmit. Therefore H is not active. This is:
options: Invalid because it uses a negative fact.
medium.hint: Would activity be compatible with no transmission?
reasoningSteps: Activity would require transmission.
The absent required result excludes activity.
medium.explanation: Activity would require transmission. The absent required result excludes activity.

medium.prompt: Every reserved bicycle has a lock. Bicycle Y is not reserved. Claim: Y has no lock. Which test defeats the claim?
medium.hint: Keep the explicit unreserved fact.
reasoningSteps: An unreserved locked bicycle violates no premise.
It shows that absence of reservation does not force absence of a lock.
medium.explanation: An unreserved locked bicycle violates no premise. It shows that absence of reservation does not force absence of a lock.

advanced.prompt: Every approved design is documented. Every documented design is archived. Design C is archived. Claim: C is approved. Which is accurate?
options: An archived unapproved design is a counterexample.
advanced.hint: The final result need not identify the initial trigger.
reasoningSteps: Both rules permit archiving designs that were never approved.
Such a design defeats the reverse conclusion.
advanced.explanation: Both rules permit archiving designs that were never approved. Such a design defeats the reverse conclusion.

advanced.prompt: Every enrolled adult in this workshop has a badge. Kira is an enrolled child with a badge. Claim: Kira is an adult. Which explains the failure?
options: The rule's adult condition cannot be inferred from a badge.
advanced.hint: A modifier remains part of the sufficient condition.
reasoningSteps: The premise restricts what enrolled adults have.
It neither prohibits children's badges nor makes a badge proof of adulthood.
advanced.explanation: The premise restricts what enrolled adults have. It neither prohibits children's badges nor makes a badge proof of adulthood.

advanced.prompt: All encrypted backups are remote. No encrypted backup is known to exist. Claim: Some remote backup exists. Which possibility defeats the claim?
options: There is an encrypted remote backup.
advanced.hint: A universal premise can hold with no qualifying cases.
reasoningSteps: With no backups, the universal rule has no counterexample.
The existential conclusion is nevertheless false.
advanced.explanation: With no backups, the universal rule has no counterexample. The existential conclusion is nevertheless false.

title: Say Exactly What Is Not True
goal: Negate a complete simple predicate without substituting an everyday opposite.
teaching: Negation denies the claim you actually have. The opposite of the room is warm is the room is not warm. The room is cold is stronger: a room can be neither warm nor cold.
Keep the subject, time and scope. The panel is approved for outdoor use becomes the panel is not approved for outdoor use. It does not become the panel is not approved for any use.

Negating a negative removes that negative: not not registered means registered. This lesson works with simple complete conditions. Negating AND/OR combinations and entire conditional rules requires the later lessons devoted to those structures.
method: Write the exact predicate being denied.
Add not to that predicate without changing its subject or scope.
Cancel a double negative when one is created.
Check that the claim and its negation cannot both be true or both be false.

statements: The package arrived before noon.
reasoning: Deny arrival before noon.
Arrival at noon, later arrival and nonarrival all fail the original claim.
workedExample.conclusion: The package did not arrive before noon.

guidedExample.prompt: What is the exact negation of The sculpture is not insured?
guidedExample.hint: Negate the existing not.
reasoningSteps: Denying not insured cancels that negative.
The result is insured, with no further claim.
guidedExample.explanation: Denying not insured cancels that negative. The result is insured, with no further claim.

commonMistake.mistake: Replacing not good with bad, or not required with forbidden.
commonMistake.repair: Deny the exact claim. Leave middle cases and different modal claims available.

beginner.prompt: Negate: The corridor is wide.
beginner.hint: Do not replace the predicate with a stronger opposite.
reasoningSteps: Not wide denies exactly wide.
Narrow and short are additional claims.
beginner.explanation: Not wide denies exactly wide. Narrow and short are additional claims.

beginner.prompt: Negate: This badge is valid.
beginner.hint: Keep this one badge as the subject.
reasoningSteps: The original concerns this badge alone.
Its denial is that this badge is not valid.
beginner.explanation: The original concerns this badge alone. Its denial is that this badge is not valid.

beginner.prompt: Negate: The key is not missing.
beginner.hint: Remove the negative you are denying.
reasoningSteps: Not missing is the full predicate.
Its negation is missing; found adds a different claim.
beginner.explanation: Not missing is the full predicate. Its negation is missing; found adds a different claim.

medium.prompt: Negate: Permit P is valid for night access.
options: P is invalid for all access.
P is not valid for night access.
P is valid for daytime access.
medium.hint: Retain the night-access restriction.
reasoningSteps: Only validity for night access is denied.
Other permissions remain unsettled.
medium.explanation: Only validity for night access is denied. Other permissions remain unsettled.

medium.prompt: Negate: Rowan must submit a report.
options: Rowan must not submit a report.
It is not required that Rowan submit a report.
Rowan did not submit a report.
medium.hint: Deny the requirement, not the action.
reasoningSteps: Not required removes the obligation.
It neither prohibits a report nor establishes noncompliance.
medium.explanation: Not required removes the obligation. It neither prohibits a report nor establishes noncompliance.

medium.prompt: Negate: The route is not unsafe.
medium.hint: Unsafe is the predicate inside not.
reasoningSteps: Denying not unsafe yields unsafe.
No separate definition equating safe with not unsafe is needed.
medium.explanation: Denying not unsafe yields unsafe. No separate definition equating safe with not unsafe is needed.

advanced.prompt: Negate: Shipment T arrived by 4 p.m. on Monday.
options: T did not arrive by 4 p.m. Monday.
advanced.hint: Nonarrival must remain a possible way to deny the original.
reasoningSteps: The exact denial retains the same deadline.
Arrival later is only one possibility; nonarrival also fits.
advanced.explanation: The exact denial retains the same deadline. Arrival later is only one possibility; nonarrival also fits.

advanced.prompt: Negate: Device J is certified to operate at temperatures below zero.
options: J is not certified to operate below zero.
J is certified only above zero.
advanced.hint: Certification and physical ability differ.
reasoningSteps: The original is about a certification.
Denying it establishes neither inability nor another certification.
advanced.explanation: The original is about a certification. Denying it establishes neither inability nor another certification.

advanced.prompt: Negate: It is not the case that Record Q is absent from the index.
options: Q is absent from the index.
Q is absent from every record system.
Q is present in the index.
advanced.hint: First identify the claim inside the outer not.
reasoningSteps: The original denies absence from this index.
Negating that denial restores absence from this same index.
advanced.explanation: The original denies absence from this index. Negating that denial restores absence from this same index.

title: Follow a Missing Requirement Backward
goal: Form an equivalent rule by reversing the conditions and negating both.
teaching: Every verified invoice is recorded. If an invoice were verified, it would have to be recorded. An invoice that is not recorded therefore cannot be verified. Verified → recorded and not recorded → not verified make the same guarantee.
To form a contrapositive, reverse the two complete conditions and negate both. Reversing alone gives an unsupported converse. Negating both without reversing gives an unsupported inverse.

Keep existing negatives and cancel double negatives. If a sensor is active, it is not silent becomes if it is silent, it is not active. Keep the same device and time throughout. A normative requirement establishes what must be done, not automatic factual compliance.

After forming a contrapositive, translate it back to English. Do not stop at symbols. For listed → not discontinued, its contrapositive is discontinued → not listed. Say it plainly: if this product is discontinued, it is not listed. That sentence checks both the negative and the direction.

Use the diagramming routine to learn and check translation. It is a training scaffold, not extra writing required on every LSAT question. Apply an obvious forward match directly. Write the contrapositive when the fact denies a result or when it exposes a hidden connection. Use notation when it makes the relationship easier to track.
method: Write both complete conditions.
Exchange their positions.
Negate each condition, cancelling double negatives.
Read the new rule in ordinary language and check the missing-required-result reasoning.

statements: Every listed product is not discontinued.
reasoning: Listed → not discontinued.
Reverse and negate: discontinued → not listed.
workedExample.conclusion: Every discontinued product is not listed.

guidedExample.prompt: Every restored clock keeps time. Which is equivalent?
options: Every clock not keeping time is not restored.
Every unrestored clock fails to keep time.
guidedExample.hint: Begin with absence of the required result.
reasoningSteps: Keeping time is required for restoration under this rule.
A clock lacking it cannot be restored.
guidedExample.explanation: Keeping time is required for restoration under this rule. A clock lacking it cannot be restored.

commonMistake.mistake: Reversing the arrow but leaving both conditions unchanged.
commonMistake.repair: Reverse and negate both. Check that the new trigger is the absence of the old required result.

beginner.prompt: Every sealed envelope is stamped. Its contrapositive is:
beginner.hint: Reverse the conditions and negate both.
reasoningSteps: Stamping is required for sealing in this rule.
No stamp therefore excludes sealing.
beginner.explanation: Stamping is required for sealing in this rule. No stamp therefore excludes sealing.

beginner.prompt: If a lamp is on, it draws current. The lamp draws no current. What follows?
beginner.hint: Use the missing required result, without inventing a cause.
reasoningSteps: Being on would require current.
No current excludes on, but does not establish why.
beginner.explanation: Being on would require current. No current excludes on, but does not establish why.

beginner.prompt: Every checked form is complete. Which is the unsupported inverse?
beginner.hint: The inverse negates without swapping.
reasoningSteps: The original starts with checked.
Not checked → not complete adds a direction the original does not guarantee.
beginner.explanation: The original starts with checked. Not checked → not complete adds a direction the original does not guarantee.

medium.prompt: If a unit is refrigerated, it is not overheated. Which is equivalent?
medium.hint: The negation of not overheated is overheated.
reasoningSteps: Swap the conditions and deny each.
The double negative on overheated cancels.
medium.explanation: Swap the conditions and deny each. The double negative on overheated cancels.

medium.prompt: If a ticket is not cancelled, it is logged. Which is equivalent?
medium.hint: Negate the original negative trigger after swapping.
reasoningSteps: No logging excludes not cancelled.
Denying not cancelled yields cancelled.
medium.explanation: No logging excludes not cancelled. Denying not cancelled yields cancelled.

medium.prompt: If a signal is not stable, it is not accepted. Which is equivalent?
medium.hint: Both negatives cancel in the contrapositive.
reasoningSteps: The old result's denial is accepted.
That requires denial of not stable, namely stable.
medium.explanation: The old result's denial is accepted. That requires denial of not stable, namely stable.

advanced.prompt: Every driver certified for Route 8 is listed on its roster. Ivo is a driver who is not listed on the Route 8 roster. Which follows?
options: Ivo is not certified for any route.
Ivo is not certified for Route 8.
advanced.hint: Preserve Route 8 in both conditions.
reasoningSteps: Ivo is a driver, so Route 8 certification would require that roster listing.
Its absence excludes only that certification.
advanced.explanation: Ivo is a driver, so Route 8 certification would require that roster listing. Its absence excludes only that certification.

advanced.prompt: Every application approved for expedited review is not missing its declaration. Which is equivalent?
options: Missing declaration → not approved for expedited review.
Not missing declaration → approved for expedited review.
Not approved for expedited review → missing declaration.
advanced.hint: Negate the whole approved-for-expedited-review condition.
reasoningSteps: Approval of this kind excludes a missing declaration.
A missing declaration therefore excludes that kind of approval.
advanced.explanation: Approval of this kind excludes a missing declaration. A missing declaration therefore excludes that kind of approval.

advanced.prompt: If the device is running at noon, its display is lit at noon. Its display is dark at midnight. What follows about noon?
options: It was not running at noon.
advanced.hint: The contrapositive must keep the original time.
reasoningSteps: The rule requires a lit display at noon.
A midnight observation does not establish the absence of that noon requirement.
advanced.explanation: The rule requires a lit display at noon. A midnight observation does not establish the absence of that noon requirement.

title: Group 3: Negate the Sufficient Idea
goal: Translate unless, until and without while retaining existing negatives and temporal scope.
teaching: The Refresher calls Group 3 negate sufficient. It includes unless, until and without in their conditional uses. The audit proceeds unless its authorization is withdrawn means not withdrawn → proceeds. Its contrapositive is not proceeds → withdrawn.

You can choose either complete idea, negate it and make it sufficient, while keeping the other unchanged. For proceeds unless authorization withdrawn, negating proceeds gives not proceeds → authorization withdrawn. The two forms are contrapositives, not competing interpretations.

Preserve negatives already in the sentence. The gate does not open without a clearance means no clearance → no opening, equivalent to opening → clearance. Until also sets a time boundary: it does not promise that the withheld action happens immediately after the boundary. Without can merely describe circumstances, so first verify what the sentence actually guarantees.

Except needs the full claim too. Every crate is retained except damaged crates guarantees not damaged → retained. It does not, by that wording alone, prove what happens to a damaged crate. If the sentence explicitly says damaged crates are discarded, that supplies a separate rule. Keep permission, prohibition, and actual events distinct when an exception concerns who may act.

Otherwise or if not can introduce the other case without making a biconditional. If a sensor resets, its log clears; otherwise its log does not clear states both cases and supports a two-way relationship between resetting and clearing. Its log clears, otherwise an alert appears supplies only not clear → alert. Translate each stated case rather than assuming both directions.
method: Identify the conditional indicator and Group 3, checking its meaning and target.
Identify the two complete ideas, including existing negatives, subjects and any time boundary.
Assign symbols to the complete ideas without dropping their qualifiers.
Apply the Group 3 rule: negate one idea on the left and keep the other unchanged on the right; cancel any resulting double negative.
Find the equivalent contrapositive by reversing and negating both complete conditions.
Translate both forms back to English and check that neither invents a guarantee from the exception.

statements: The meeting proceeds unless its venue becomes unavailable.
reasoning: Choose venue becomes unavailable and negate it.
No venue unavailability → meeting proceeds.
The equivalent direction is meeting does not proceed → venue becomes unavailable.
workedExample.conclusion: A venue becoming unavailable does not by itself prove cancellation.

guidedExample.prompt: The pump fails without coolant. Which is guaranteed?
options: Coolant present → pump does not fail.
guidedExample.hint: Without supplies the absent condition that triggers failure.
reasoningSteps: Coolant absence is sufficient for failure.
Presence may still coexist with failure from another cause.
guidedExample.explanation: Coolant absence is sufficient for failure. Presence may still coexist with failure from another cause.

commonMistake.mistake: Making unless exclusive or treating the exception as guaranteed success.
commonMistake.repair: Translate the stated guarantee and its contrapositive. Do not add a reverse or a promise about what happens once the exception occurs.

beginner.prompt: The delivery proceeds unless the road closes. Translate.
options: Road closed → delivery does not proceed.
beginner.hint: Negate road closes and keep proceeds unchanged.
reasoningSteps: The rule promises delivery when closure is absent.
It does not establish the outcome when closure occurs.
beginner.explanation: The rule promises delivery when closure is absent. It does not establish the outcome when closure occurs.

beginner.prompt: The display dims without external power. Which follows?
beginner.hint: Start with absence of external power.
reasoningSteps: Without external power supplies the sufficient condition.
The result is dimming, without excluding other causes.
beginner.explanation: Without external power supplies the sufficient condition. The result is dimming, without excluding other causes.

beginner.prompt: The briefing ends unless another speaker arrives. No other speaker arrives. What follows?
beginner.hint: Use the nonexception case.
reasoningSteps: No arrival meets the negated exception.
The promised ending follows.
beginner.explanation: No arrival meets the negated exception. The promised ending follows.

medium.prompt: The ticket is not issued without identification. Which is equivalent?
medium.hint: First write no identification → not issued.
reasoningSteps: Negating the not-issued result gives issued.
Its contrapositive requires identification.
medium.explanation: Negating the not-issued result gives issued. Its contrapositive requires identification.

medium.prompt: Unless the upload fails, the receipt appears. No receipt appears. What follows?
medium.hint: Use the contrapositive of no failure → receipt appears.
reasoningSteps: Receipt absence excludes no upload failure.
It therefore establishes failure under the stated rule, not a different explanation.
medium.explanation: Receipt absence excludes no upload failure. It therefore establishes failure under the stated rule, not a different explanation.

medium.prompt: Lena does not sign until the price is fixed. The price has been fixed. What follows?
options: Whether Lena signs is still unknown.
medium.hint: Removing a barrier is not a promise to act.
reasoningSteps: The rule bars signing before the price is fixed.
It does not guarantee signing after fixation.
medium.explanation: The rule bars signing before the price is fixed. It does not guarantee signing after fixation.

advanced.prompt: Unless the parcel is not cleared for export, it is loaded. It is not loaded. Which follows?
options: The parcel is not cleared for export.
The parcel is cleared for export.
The parcel is not cleared for any use.
advanced.hint: Negating not cleared gives cleared as the original trigger.
reasoningSteps: Cleared for export → loaded.
No loading therefore gives not cleared for export, retaining that scope.
advanced.explanation: Cleared for export → loaded. No loading therefore gives not cleared for export, retaining that scope.

advanced.prompt: At a site, no repair begins until that site's inspection is complete. A repair begins at Site K. What follows?
options: Site K's inspection caused the repair.
advanced.hint: Keep the site identity in the temporal requirement.
reasoningSteps: A repair at K requires the boundary condition for K.
Neither inspections elsewhere nor causation is established.
advanced.explanation: A repair at K requires the boundary condition for K. Neither inspections elsewhere nor causation is established.

advanced.prompt: The technician described a visit without her assistant. What conditional rule follows from this sentence alone?
advanced.hint: Does without express a general guarantee here?
reasoningSteps: The sentence describes the circumstances of a particular visit.
It supplies no exceptionless rule about other visits.
advanced.explanation: The sentence describes the circumstances of a particular visit. It supplies no exceptionless rule about other visits.

title: Group 4: Keep Two Conditions Apart
goal: Translate exclusions as a sufficient condition requiring the other condition's absence.
teaching: Group 4 in the Refresher is negate necessary: no, none, not both, never and cannot in their relevant uses. No archived sample is disposable gives archived sample → not disposable. Choosing disposable as the trigger gives disposable → not archived sample.

Not both says two conditions cannot occur together. The west hatch and the east hatch are not both open gives west open → east not open and east open → west not open. It permits both to be closed. It does not require exactly one to be open.

Never and cannot need context. A descriptive rule that the device never runs uncooled excludes that combination. An instruction that a visitor cannot enter means entry is forbidden; it does not physically prevent an unauthorized entry. Keep the claim's modal meaning rather than changing permission into behavior.

Not can negate a result inside a universal rule: Paper forms are not accepted means paper form → not accepted. The word not alone does not create a universal rule. This form was not accepted is a case fact, and not all paper forms are accepted says at least one is unaccepted. Read the whole scope before applying the exclusion procedure.
method: Identify the exclusion indicator and Group 4, checking exactly what coexistence is forbidden.
Identify the two complete conditions that cannot coexist, preserving subjects, qualifiers and existing negatives.
Assign symbols to those complete conditions.
Apply the Group 4 rule: keep one unchanged on the left and negate the other on the right; cancel any resulting double negative.
Find the equivalent contrapositive by reversing and negating both complete conditions.
Translate both forms back to English and check that the rule excludes coexistence without inventing existence or an exactly-one requirement.

statements: No reusable vial is marked for disposal.
reasoning: Reusable vial → not marked for disposal.
Marked for disposal → not reusable vial is equivalent.
workedExample.conclusion: The two categories do not overlap; neither category is asserted to have members.

guidedExample.prompt: The front pump and rear pump are not both active. Which case is allowed?
guidedExample.hint: Not both does not mean at least one.
reasoningSteps: The rule excludes joint activity.
Joint inactivity violates no stated condition.
guidedExample.explanation: The rule excludes joint activity. Joint inactivity violates no stated condition.

commonMistake.mistake: Reading no overlap as exactly one condition must hold.
commonMistake.repair: State the prohibited combination. Ask whether the rule also supplied an at-least-one claim; if it did not, allow neither.

beginner.prompt: No rented instrument is for sale. Which translates this?
beginner.hint: Keep rented unchanged; deny the excluded property.
reasoningSteps: Rental and for-sale status cannot coexist.
The rule does not assign sale status to nonrentals.
beginner.explanation: Rental and for-sale status cannot coexist. The rule does not assign sale status to nonrentals.

beginner.prompt: None of the overnight shipments are uninsured. What follows for an overnight shipment?
beginner.hint: Negate uninsured as not insured.
reasoningSteps: Overnight shipment → not uninsured.
Using uninsured to mean not insured, the double negative yields insured.
beginner.explanation: Overnight shipment → not uninsured. Using uninsured to mean not insured, the double negative yields insured.

beginner.prompt: A recorder never stores an unverified clip. Which follows?
beginner.hint: Storage excludes being unverified.
reasoningSteps: The forbidden pair is stored and unverified.
A stored clip therefore must be verified under this descriptive rule.
beginner.explanation: The forbidden pair is stored and unverified. A stored clip therefore must be verified under this descriptive rule.

medium.prompt: The gallery and workshop are not both open. The gallery is closed. What follows about the workshop?
medium.hint: Only joint opening is excluded.
reasoningSteps: The gallery's closure removes the prohibited combination.
The workshop may be open or closed.
medium.explanation: The gallery's closure removes the prohibited combination. The workshop may be open or closed.

medium.prompt: No locked folder is publicly readable. Folder C is publicly readable. What follows?
medium.hint: Use the equivalent exclusion from the other direction.
reasoningSteps: Public readability cannot coexist with locking.
C's readability therefore excludes locking.
medium.explanation: Public readability cannot coexist with locking. C's readability therefore excludes locking.

medium.prompt: No metal tool approved for this scan is magnetic. Which condition belongs on the left?
options: Metal tool approved for this scan.
medium.hint: Retain the approval modifier.
reasoningSteps: Only the specified approved metal tools are excluded from magnetism.
Dropping approval would extend the rule to other tools.
medium.explanation: Only the specified approved metal tools are excluded from magnetism. Dropping approval would extend the rule to other tools.

advanced.prompt: No equipment not certified for outdoor use is deployed outdoors. Which follows?
options: Deployed outdoors → certified for outdoor use.
Certified for outdoor use → deployed outdoors.
advanced.hint: Write not certified → not deployed, then contrapose.
reasoningSteps: Outdoor deployment excludes absence of outdoor certification.
The resulting positive certification retains its original scope.
advanced.explanation: Outdoor deployment excludes absence of outdoor certification. The resulting positive certification retains its original scope.

advanced.prompt: The policy says visitors cannot enter the vault. A visitor enters. Which follows about that event?
options: The entrant cannot be a visitor.
advanced.hint: The policy establishes a prohibition, not factual compliance.
reasoningSteps: The visitor is subject to the entry prohibition.
The event breaches that prohibition without changing the person's status.
advanced.explanation: The visitor is subject to the entry prohibition. The event breaches that prohibition without changing the person's status.

advanced.prompt: No artwork on loan is insured by the museum's local policy. Which follows from the rule alone?
options: Some artwork has no insurance at all.
On-loan artwork is not insured by that local policy; existence is not established.
All artwork without local insurance is on loan.
advanced.hint: Keep both the insurance scope and the absence of an existence fact.
reasoningSteps: The exclusion concerns one named policy.
It establishes neither an existing artwork nor absence of other insurance.
advanced.explanation: The exclusion concerns one named policy. It establishes neither an existing artwork nor absence of other insurance.

title: Choose the Direction from the Meaning
goal: Select the appropriate translation procedure without relying on a single familiar word.
teaching: Mixed practice asks you to read the relationship before choosing a procedure. If a hearing is televised, it is recorded puts televised left. A hearing is televised only if it is recorded has the same direction, although the wording points you to a necessary condition.

A hearing is not televised without a recording also gives televised → recorded. No televised hearing is unrecorded excludes the same forbidden combination. Different indicator groups can express equivalent relationships.

Keep full predicates before abbreviating. Approved for trial use differs from approved for routine use. A word such as only or without is evidence about structure, not permission to discard modifiers, existing negatives or obligations.
method: Identify the indicator and group, using the What Test when its target is unclear.
Identify both complete ideas, preserving subjects, scope and existing negatives.
Assign symbols to the complete ideas.
Apply the matching group translation rule; use a Personalized If/Then to check the meaning.
Find the contrapositive, reversing and negating each complete condition.
Recall and Rephrase: put the guide aside, write both forms in English, then compare with the original and explain any correction.

statements: Only documents cleared for public release appear on the portal.
reasoning: The restricted event is appearing on the portal.
Its necessary condition is clearance for public release.
workedExample.conclusion: Document appears on portal → document cleared for public release.

guidedExample.prompt: The server does not restart unless its update is complete. Which is equivalent?
options: Server does not restart → update incomplete.
guidedExample.hint: Write update incomplete → no restart first.
reasoningSteps: Incomplete update prevents restart.
Its contrapositive makes completed update necessary for restart, not sufficient.
guidedExample.explanation: Incomplete update prevents restart. Its contrapositive makes completed update necessary for restart, not sufficient.

commonMistake.mistake: Choosing an arrow from the first keyword without rereading the claim.
commonMistake.repair: Read the proposed arrow as a complete English sentence. Check whether it adds a reverse guarantee or changes a negative.

beginner.prompt: Every inspected ladder has a tag. Choose the equivalent statement.
options: If a ladder is inspected, it has a tag.
An uninspected ladder has no tag.
beginner.hint: Every introduces the sufficient group.
reasoningSteps: Inspection is sufficient for tagging.
Neither the reverse nor the inverse is supplied.
beginner.explanation: Inspection is sufficient for tagging. Neither the reverse nor the inverse is supplied.

beginner.prompt: Only stamped forms are accepted. Translate.
beginner.hint: Only restricts the accepted group.
reasoningSteps: Acceptance requires stamping.
Stamping alone is not a guarantee of acceptance.
beginner.explanation: Acceptance requires stamping. Stamping alone is not a guarantee of acceptance.

beginner.prompt: No transparent container is opaque. Which follows?
beginner.hint: This is an exclusion, not a complete division into two groups.
reasoningSteps: Transparency excludes opacity.
The rule gives no exhaustive classification of other containers.
beginner.explanation: Transparency excludes opacity. The rule gives no exhaustive classification of other containers.

medium.prompt: The exhibit remains open unless the alarm is activated. Which is equivalent?
medium.hint: Translate no activation → open, then contrapose.
reasoningSteps: No activation guarantees openness.
Lack of openness therefore requires activation, but activation alone does not prove closure.
medium.explanation: No activation guarantees openness. Lack of openness therefore requires activation, but activation alone does not prove closure.

medium.prompt: The only bids selected are bids with a deposit. Which inference is unsupported?
medium.hint: A deposit is required, not promised sufficient.
reasoningSteps: The restriction gives selected → deposit and its contrapositive.
The reverse would make every deposit-bearing bid selected without support.
medium.explanation: The restriction gives selected → deposit and its contrapositive. The reverse would make every deposit-bearing bid selected without support.

medium.prompt: Without verification, the transfer is not processed. The transfer is processed. What follows?
medium.hint: Existing not processed stays negative in the first arrow.
reasoningSteps: No verification → no processing.
Processing therefore requires verification.
medium.explanation: No verification → no processing. Processing therefore requires verification.

advanced.prompt: No proposal not approved for the pilot is implemented in the pilot. Which translation is equivalent?
options: Implemented in pilot → approved for pilot.
Approved for pilot → implemented in pilot.
advanced.hint: Cancel double negatives without broadening implementation scope.
reasoningSteps: Not approved for pilot → not implemented in pilot.
Its contrapositive is pilot implementation → pilot approval.
advanced.explanation: Not approved for pilot → not implemented in pilot. Its contrapositive is pilot implementation → pilot approval.

advanced.prompt: Only applicants licensed in Region N qualify for this role. Kai is licensed in Region M. No other license information is given. What follows?
advanced.hint: A license in M does not exclude also having a license in N.
reasoningSteps: The role requires Region N licensing.
The fact about M establishes neither N licensing nor its absence.
advanced.explanation: The role requires Region N licensing. The fact about M establishes neither N licensing nor its absence.

advanced.prompt: The agency requires every field observer to carry a beacon. Which claim keeps the statement's force?
options: Every field observer actually carries a beacon.
Every field observer is obliged to carry a beacon.
Anyone carrying a beacon is a field observer.
advanced.hint: Requirements and performance are different predicates.
reasoningSteps: The agency imposes an obligation on field observers.
The statement does not guarantee compliance or identify beacon carriers.
advanced.explanation: The agency imposes an obligation on field observers. The statement does not guarantee compliance or identify beacon carriers.

title: Recognize a Guarantee without a Familiar Indicator
goal: Translate guarantees expressed through verbs, definitions and restricted subjects.
teaching: The relationship can appear without if or only if. A certified seal guarantees traceability gives certified seal → traceability. Traceability is a prerequisite for listing gives listed → traceable. Ask what the sentence makes enough and what it makes required.

Definitions can supply both directions, but only when the definition is explicit. Here, a dormant account means an account with no transactions for a year identifies the defined category. Do not turn a loose description such as dormant accounts tend to be old into a definition or an exceptionless rule.

Preserve the distinction between guarantee, permission and evidence. A grant authorizes travel gives a permission; it does not prove the traveler leaves. A wet pavement suggests rain does not guarantee rain. Active and passive phrasing can express the same rule without changing the subject involved.
method: Find the guarantee, prerequisite, exclusion or explicit definition.
Write what is enough and what is required in complete predicates.
Retain the force of verbs such as authorizes, suggests and requires.
Test whether a counterexample would violate the actual wording.

statements: A checksum match ensures that the stored copy is intact.
reasoning: The match supplies a guarantee, rather than a mere clue.
The result concerns the stored copy's integrity.
workedExample.conclusion: Checksum matches → stored copy intact.

guidedExample.prompt: Identity verification is a prerequisite for issuing a replacement card. Which follows?
guidedExample.hint: A prerequisite must be met for the restricted outcome.
reasoningSteps: Issuance requires verification.
Verification is not stated sufficient for issuance.
guidedExample.explanation: Issuance requires verification. Verification is not stated sufficient for issuance.

commonMistake.mistake: Treating any association as a guarantee.
commonMistake.repair: Compare ensures with suggests. Translate the author's degree of commitment, not a stronger relationship.

beginner.prompt: A successful self-test guarantees that the indicator lights. Choose the rule.
options: Self-test fails → indicator does not light.
beginner.hint: Guarantees identifies the sufficient event.
reasoningSteps: Self-test success supplies the guarantee.
The sentence leaves other ways to light the indicator open.
beginner.explanation: Self-test success supplies the guarantee. The sentence leaves other ways to light the indicator open.

beginner.prompt: A signature is a prerequisite for approval. Which follows?
beginner.hint: A prerequisite belongs on the necessary side.
reasoningSteps: Approval requires a signature.
A signature alone is not declared sufficient.
beginner.explanation: Approval requires a signature. A signature alone is not declared sufficient.

beginner.prompt: A valid access token ensures successful entry. Entry is unsuccessful. What follows?
options: The entrant was not a person.
beginner.hint: Apply absence of the guaranteed result.
reasoningSteps: A valid token would ensure entry.
Unsuccessful entry excludes token validity under this stipulated rule.
beginner.explanation: A valid token would ensure entry. Unsuccessful entry excludes token validity under this stipulated rule.

medium.prompt: A sealed housing is ensured by factory certification. Which is the direction?
medium.hint: By identifies the source of the guarantee in this passive sentence.
reasoningSteps: Factory certification is what ensures sealing.
The passive phrasing does not reverse that relationship.
medium.explanation: Factory certification is what ensures sealing. The passive phrasing does not reverse that relationship.

medium.prompt: Residue on a filter suggests that the intake was blocked. What rule is established?
medium.hint: Suggests is weaker than guarantees.
reasoningSteps: The statement treats residue as evidence.
It does not rule out residue without blockage or blockage without residue.
medium.explanation: The statement treats residue as evidence. It does not rule out residue without blockage or blockage without residue.

medium.prompt: A digital pass authorizes its holder to use the express lane. Which follows for a holder?
options: The holder is authorized to use the lane.
Everyone using the lane has a digital pass.
medium.hint: Keep authorizes in the result.
reasoningSteps: Holding the pass guarantees the stated authorization.
It establishes neither exercise of that permission nor an exclusive source of permission.
medium.explanation: Holding the pass guarantees the stated authorization. It establishes neither exercise of that permission nor an exclusive source of permission.

advanced.prompt: A device's eligibility for the rebate depends on certification for indoor operation. Device T is certified only for outdoor operation. What follows?
advanced.hint: Only outdoor means the required indoor certification is absent.
reasoningSteps: Eligibility requires indoor certification.
The stated restriction to outdoor certification excludes that requirement.
advanced.explanation: Eligibility requires indoor certification. The stated restriction to outdoor certification excludes that requirement.

advanced.prompt: In this catalogue, a pending record is defined as a record awaiting review. Record B awaits review. What follows?
options: B is a pending record under this definition.
advanced.hint: An explicit definition applies within its stated setting.
reasoningSteps: The catalogue definition identifies awaiting-review records as pending.
It applies to B without extending the definition to other catalogues.
advanced.explanation: The catalogue definition identifies awaiting-review records as pending. It applies to B without extending the definition to other catalogues.

advanced.prompt: A transfer's completion is contingent on the receiving bank accepting it. The receiving bank accepted Transfer L. Which follows?
advanced.hint: Contingent on states a requirement rather than a sufficient cause.
reasoningSteps: Completion requires acceptance.
Acceptance alone does not rule out other barriers to completion.
advanced.explanation: Completion requires acceptance. Acceptance alone does not rule out other barriers to completion.

title: Connect Rules through the Same Condition
goal: Build a directed chain and distinguish its new conditional from a case conclusion.
teaching: Every calibrated meter is registered. Every registered meter is listed. A calibrated meter must therefore be listed: calibrated → registered → listed. The middle condition matches exactly and the arrows continue in the same direction.
That chain creates a rule, not an existing calibrated meter. Meter D is calibrated adds the fact needed to conclude that D is listed. A listed meter alone does not prove calibration.

Match complete meanings, not shared words. Registered for field use differs from registered for laboratory use. Keep the same subject through the chain. Rules concerning an object's owner or maker do not automatically transfer that property back to the object.

A link can be hidden until you take a contrapositive. Every tagged specimen is retained. Every discarded specimen is not retained. The second rule is equivalent to retained → not discarded. Now tagged → retained → not discarded is a forward chain. Write the equivalent rule first; do not simply reverse an arrow. If both sides already contain negatives, cancel the double negatives when contraposing.

Build the chain visibly before compressing it. Write calibrated → registered and registered → listed on separate lines. Align the repeated registered condition so that the first arrow arrives where the next arrow begins. Follow the path to calibrated → listed. Keep branches in the available space; a shared result with two incoming arrows is not a forward bridge.

A longer chain supports intermediate connections too. For calibrated → registered → listed → indexed, calibrated → listed, registered → indexed, and calibrated → indexed all follow. An answer need not connect the first and last ideas. Start with the proposed answer's trigger and check whether a forward path reaches its exact result.

Compare these complete middle conditions: late submission → requires approval; received approval → issued a reference number. They do not link. Requires approval and received approval differ, even though approval appears in both. A late submission still awaiting approval fits both rules without a reference number, so that proposed conclusion is not guaranteed.
method: Translate each rule into complete conditions.
Find a result-to-trigger match; if needed, form an equivalent contrapositive to expose it.
Follow only forward arrows in the rules or their valid contrapositives to create a new rule.
Apply a separately supplied case fact, or preserve the result as a rule if no fact is given.

statements: Every audited report is certified.
Every certified report is published.
Report R is audited.
reasoning: Audited → certified → published.
R satisfies the first condition, so both required results follow for R.
workedExample.conclusion: Report R is certified and published.

guidedExample.prompt: Every keyed cabinet is numbered. Every numbered cabinet is catalogued. Which follows from these rules alone?
guidedExample.hint: Link the shared numbered condition without adding a case.
reasoningSteps: Keyed leads to numbered and then catalogued.
The result is a new conditional, without existence or a reverse direction.
guidedExample.explanation: Keyed leads to numbered and then catalogued. The result is a new conditional, without existence or a reverse direction.

commonMistake.mistake: Joining rules merely because they use similar nouns.
commonMistake.repair: Compare the full middle predicates and subject identities. A link needs the same condition, not a related topic.

beginner.prompt: Every glazed tile is polished. Every polished tile is inspected. What follows?
beginner.hint: Follow the polished middle condition.
reasoningSteps: Glazing guarantees polishing.
Polishing guarantees inspection, so glazing guarantees inspection.
beginner.explanation: Glazing guarantees polishing. Polishing guarantees inspection, so glazing guarantees inspection.

beginner.prompt: Every sealed bottle is labelled. Every labelled bottle is boxed. Bottle A is sealed. What follows?
options: A is the only boxed bottle.
beginner.hint: Move A forward through both rules.
reasoningSteps: A's sealing gives labelling.
That labelling gives boxing, without identifying other bottles.
beginner.explanation: A's sealing gives labelling. That labelling gives boxing, without identifying other bottles.

beginner.prompt: Every enrolled intern is assigned a desk. Every person assigned a desk has an entry code. Which is the middle condition?
options: Being an intern regardless of enrollment.
beginner.hint: Find the first rule's result repeated as the second trigger.
reasoningSteps: Desk assignment is the shared condition.
It connects enrolled interns to entry codes.
beginner.explanation: Desk assignment is the shared condition. It connects enrolled interns to entry codes.

medium.prompt: Every registered instrument is calibrated. Every calibrated instrument is tagged. Instrument Q is tagged. What follows about registration?
medium.hint: Being at the end of a chain does not establish its beginning.
reasoningSteps: Registration guarantees tagging through calibration.
Tagging may also occur without registration.
medium.explanation: Registration guarantees tagging through calibration. Tagging may also occur without registration.

medium.prompt: Every compact sensor is portable. Every portable sensor is battery-powered. No compact sensor is known to exist. Which follows?
medium.hint: Preserve the output as a rule.
reasoningSteps: Compact → portable → battery-powered.
No case fact supports an existence conclusion.
medium.explanation: Compact → portable → battery-powered. No case fact supports an existence conclusion.

medium.prompt: Every archived file is signed. Every restricted file is unsigned. Which new rule follows?
medium.hint: Contrapose restricted → not signed to expose a signed trigger.
reasoningSteps: Restricted → not signed has the equivalent form signed → not restricted.
Archived → signed now links to signed → not restricted, so archived → not restricted.
medium.explanation: Restricted → not signed has the equivalent form signed → not restricted. Archived → signed now links to signed → not restricted, so archived → not restricted.

advanced.prompt: Every vessel certified for coastal service is entered in Register C. Every vessel entered in Register C is assigned an identifier. Vessel R is certified for coastal service. Which follows?
options: R is certified for ocean service.
advanced.hint: Retain coastal certification and follow the exact register match.
reasoningSteps: Coastal certification gives Register C entry.
That entry gives R an identifier, without another certification or a reverse rule.
advanced.explanation: Coastal certification gives Register C entry. That entry gives R an identifier, without another certification or a reverse rule.

advanced.prompt: Every authorized visitor may request a transcript. Everyone who may request a transcript receives a request code. Jo is an authorized visitor. What follows?
advanced.hint: The middle condition is permission to request, not an actual request.
reasoningSteps: Jo satisfies the complete authorized-visitor condition and receives permission to request.
The second rule explicitly applies to that permission and yields a request code.
advanced.explanation: Jo satisfies the complete authorized-visitor condition and receives permission to request. The second rule explicitly applies to that permission and yields a request code.

advanced.prompt: Every field-certified sensor is logged. Every uncalibrated sensor is unlogged. Every calibrated sensor has an identifier. Sensor F is field-certified. What follows?
options: F is calibrated and has an identifier.
F is uncalibrated and has no identifier.
advanced.hint: Expose a logged → calibrated link by contraposing the uncalibrated rule.
reasoningSteps: Uncalibrated → not logged becomes logged → calibrated after reversal and double-negation cancellation.
F follows field-certified → logged → calibrated → has an identifier. No reverse identifier rule is supplied.
advanced.explanation: Uncalibrated → not logged becomes logged → calibrated after reversal and double-negation cancellation. F follows field-certified → logged → calibrated → has an identifier. No reverse identifier rule is supplied.

title: Know When Rules Do Not Connect
goal: Reject false links caused by shared results, shared triggers, scope changes or subject changes.
teaching: Every trained guide is insured. Every licensed guide is insured. Both rules end at insured. They do not establish that trained guides are licensed or licensed guides are trained. Insurance can be shared by different groups.

A shared trigger produces two results, not a new relationship between those results. Every approved item is tagged and every approved item is boxed establish both results for an approved item. They do not establish tagged → boxed for all items.

An apparent mismatch may be real or may be resolved by a valid contrapositive. Check exact scope and subjects before declaring no link. The preceding linking lesson showed how contraposition exposes hidden connections. Use that procedure before deciding that a shared word supplies no valid path.

Check the requirement-versus-completion distinction explicitly. Late application → requires approval does not meet received approval → has a signature. A late application awaiting approval is a counterexample to the claim that it must have a signature. Nothing in the two rules says its requirement has been fulfilled.
method: Write the direction of each rule.
Compare complete predicates, including qualifiers and subjects.
Look for an actual result-to-trigger connection, including a taught equivalent form.
If none exists, preserve separate rules and draw only conclusions supported by any case fact.

statements: Every approved device is registered.
Every inspected device is registered.
Device J is approved.
reasoning: Approval gives registration for J.
Registration is also a result of inspection, not proof of inspection.
workedExample.conclusion: J is registered; inspection remains unknown.

guidedExample.prompt: Every red folder is indexed. Every blue folder is indexed. Which follows?
options: Every indexed folder is red or blue.
guidedExample.hint: A shared result does not connect the starting groups.
reasoningSteps: Both colors imply indexing.
The rules allow indexed folders of other colors and do not identify one color with the other.
guidedExample.explanation: Both colors imply indexing. The rules allow indexed folders of other colors and do not identify one color with the other.

commonMistake.mistake: Turning a common result into a bridge between its possible sources.
commonMistake.repair: Draw the arrows. Two arrowheads meeting at a result do not provide a forward path from one source to the other.

beginner.prompt: Every bronze medal is numbered. Every silver medal is numbered. Does bronze imply silver?
options: No; the shared result supplies no such link.
Yes, if no medal fact is supplied.
beginner.hint: Both arrows point toward numbered.
reasoningSteps: Numbering can result from either medal category.
It does not establish a connection between those categories.
beginner.explanation: Numbering can result from either medal category. It does not establish a connection between those categories.

beginner.prompt: Every registered boat is painted. Every registered boat is inspected. Which follows for a registered boat?
beginner.hint: Apply both rules to the same supplied trigger.
reasoningSteps: Registration guarantees both results.
The shared trigger does not link all painted boats to inspection.
beginner.explanation: Registration guarantees both results. The shared trigger does not link all painted boats to inspection.

beginner.prompt: Every approved poster is mounted. Every laminated poster is mounted. Poster D is approved. What follows?
beginner.hint: Use D's actual sufficient condition.
reasoningSteps: Approval guarantees mounting.
The lamination rule has no established trigger for D.
beginner.explanation: Approval guarantees mounting. The lamination rule has no established trigger for D.

medium.prompt: Every battery tested at Site A is labelled. Every battery tested at Site B is shipped. Battery J was tested at A. What follows?
options: J was labelled; shipping remains unknown.
Testing at A is the same condition as testing at B.
medium.hint: The site qualifier changes the predicate.
reasoningSteps: J meets only the supplied Site A trigger.
The Site B rule cannot be activated without Site B testing.
medium.explanation: J meets only the supplied Site A trigger. The Site B rule cannot be activated without Site B testing.

medium.prompt: Every certified helmet has padding. Every certified helmet has a serial number. A helmet has padding. Which follows about its serial number?
medium.hint: Padding is a result, not the shared trigger.
reasoningSteps: Padding alone does not establish certification.
Without certification, the serial-number rule has no confirmed trigger.
medium.explanation: Padding alone does not establish certification. Without certification, the serial-number rule has no confirmed trigger.

medium.prompt: Every catalogued specimen is photographed. Every photographed specimen is labelled for storage. Is there a link?
medium.hint: Do not reject a genuine result-to-trigger match.
reasoningSteps: Photographed connects the two rules directly.
The path runs from cataloguing to storage labelling, not backward.
medium.explanation: Photographed connects the two rules directly. The path runs from cataloguing to storage labelling, not backward.

advanced.prompt: Every inspected vehicle has an authorized owner. Every authorized owner holds a permit. Which follows?
options: Every inspected vehicle holds a permit.
The owner of every inspected vehicle holds a permit.
Every permitted owner has an inspected vehicle.
advanced.hint: Track which subject receives the second property.
reasoningSteps: Inspection establishes authorization of that vehicle's owner.
The permit belongs to the owner, not automatically to the vehicle.
advanced.explanation: Inspection establishes authorization of that vehicle's owner. The permit belongs to the owner, not automatically to the vehicle.

advanced.prompt: Every sample documented in the research register is retained. Every sample certified for export is documented in the export register. Which link is justified without another premise?
options: Neither: documentation in the two different registers is not the same condition.
advanced.hint: Compare the complete register-specific predicates.
reasoningSteps: The second result is documentation in the export register.
The first trigger requires documentation in the research register, and no rule connects them.
advanced.explanation: The second result is documentation in the export register. The first trigger requires documentation in the research register, and no rule connects them.

advanced.prompt: Every active terminal is connected. Every connected terminal is logged. Terminal R is not active. Which follows?
advanced.hint: The absence of the first trigger does not settle later results.
reasoningSteps: The chain guarantees logging for active terminals.
Inactive terminals may be connected and logged, or neither, consistently with both rules.
advanced.explanation: The chain guarantees logging for active terminals. Inactive terminals may be connected and logged, or neither, consistently with both rules.

title: Know when a rule fires
goal: Apply a rule to established facts without assuming its trigger.
teaching: A rule and a fact do different jobs. If every approved order is dispatched, the rule does not tell us that any order is approved. An approved order supplies the trigger; then dispatch follows.
A fact about the necessary condition does not fire the rule backward. A negative fact about that condition can fire the contrapositive. Keep the same order, person or event throughout the inference.
method: Write the complete trigger and result.
List only established facts about the same subject.
Match a fact to the trigger, or to the trigger of the contrapositive.
State the result and leave every untriggered rule open.

statements: Every refrigerated parcel gets a blue label.
Parcel J is refrigerated.
reasoning: Refrigerated → blue label.
J satisfies the sufficient condition.
workedExample.conclusion: Parcel J gets a blue label.

commonMistake.mistake: The rule exists, so its trigger must occur.
commonMistake.repair: A rule constrains qualifying cases. Supply a qualifying fact before asserting a result.

guidedExample.prompt: Every verified account can upload. Account T can upload. What follows?
guidedExample.explanation: Upload is the result, not the trigger. Both verified and unverified accounts might upload.
guidedExample.hint: Which side of verified → upload is given?
reasoningSteps: Which side of verified → upload is given?
Upload is the result, not the trigger.
Both verified and unverified accounts might upload.

beginner.prompt: Every tagged bag is inspected. Bag K is tagged. What follows?
beginner.explanation: Tagged is the trigger and K satisfies it.
beginner.hint: Match the given fact to the left side.
reasoningSteps: Match the given fact to the left side.
Tagged is the trigger and K satisfies it.

beginner.prompt: If a lamp is solar powered, it needs no outlet. This lamp needs an outlet. What follows?
beginner.explanation: Needing an outlet denies the required result. The contrapositive rules out solar power.
beginner.hint: Use the negative of the necessary condition.
reasoningSteps: Use the negative of the necessary condition.
Needing an outlet denies the required result.
The contrapositive rules out solar power.

beginner.prompt: Every archived message is searchable. Message M is searchable. Is it archived?
beginner.explanation: Searchable messages may have other sources. The rule gives only one direction.
beginner.hint: A result alone does not establish its cause or trigger.
reasoningSteps: A result alone does not establish its cause or trigger.
Searchable messages may have other sources.
The rule gives only one direction.

medium.prompt: Every signed form is filed. Every filed form is numbered. Form Z is signed. What follows?
options: Z is numbered but need not be filed.
medium.explanation: The signed fact fires the first rule; the resulting filed fact fires the second.
medium.hint: Carry the first result into the next trigger.
reasoningSteps: Carry the first result into the next trigger.
The signed fact fires the first rule; the resulting filed fact fires the second.

medium.prompt: Audited accounts have records. P lacks records; Q has records. Which is established?
options: Neither P nor Q is audited.
P is not audited; Q remains undecided.
Q is audited; P remains undecided.
medium.explanation: The missing required records rule out auditing for P. Records alone do not prove auditing for Q.
medium.hint: Apply the rule separately to each account.
reasoningSteps: Apply the rule separately to each account.
The missing required records rule out auditing for P.
Records alone do not prove auditing for Q.

medium.prompt: Every trained guide is certified. Every certified guide is listed. Eli is not listed. What follows?
options: Eli is neither certified nor trained.
medium.explanation: Not listed gives not certified; not certified gives not trained.
medium.hint: Run the chain backward using contrapositives.
reasoningSteps: Run the chain backward using contrapositives.
Not listed gives not certified; not certified gives not trained.

advanced.prompt: All approved designs use recycled steel. All coastal designs are approved. Design X uses recycled steel. What is known?
options: X may be coastal, but this is not established.
advanced.explanation: Steel is the end of coastal → approved → recycled steel. It does not prove the beginning.
advanced.hint: Which facts would actually start the chain?
reasoningSteps: Which facts would actually start the chain?
Steel is the end of coastal → approved → recycled steel.
It does not prove the beginning.

advanced.prompt: Every screened visitor receives a badge. Every badged visitor may enter. Visitor R may enter; visitor S has no badge. What follows?
options: R and S were both screened.
S was not screened; R may or may not have been screened.
R was screened and S may enter.
advanced.explanation: S denies a necessary condition of screening. Entry for R is only a result and does not prove screening.
advanced.hint: Do not transfer one visitor’s fact to the other.
reasoningSteps: Do not transfer one visitor’s fact to the other.
S denies a necessary condition of screening.
Entry for R is only a result and does not prove screening.

advanced.prompt: Every project with a valid restoration permit has a completed restoration survey. Every project with a completed restoration survey has an access plan. Project L has no access plan. Does L have a valid restoration permit?
options: Yes, because no survey is mentioned.
Survey completion cannot affect permit validity.
advanced.explanation: A valid permit guarantees a completed restoration survey, which guarantees an access plan. L lacks that result, so valid permit status is ruled out. These descriptive premises establish actual conditions, not merely obligations.
advanced.hint: Follow valid permit → completed restoration survey → access plan for the same project.
reasoningSteps: Follow valid permit → completed restoration survey → access plan for the same project.
A valid permit guarantees a completed restoration survey, which guarantees an access plan.
L lacks that result, so valid permit status is ruled out.
These descriptive premises establish actual conditions, not merely obligations.

title: Keep AND and OR inside the right scope
goal: Distinguish joint requirements from alternative routes.
teaching: AND requires both listed conditions. OR permits at least one and ordinarily permits both. In (license AND insurance) → entry, neither license alone nor insurance alone establishes entry.

Scope matters. A → (B OR C) gives alternatives in the result. (A OR B) → C supplies two separate routes to C. A → (B AND C) requires both results. Do not replace a complete phrase with one convenient word.
method: Bracket the complete sufficient and necessary sides.
Read AND as both; read OR as at least one.
For a joint trigger, establish every part.

title: Find what the argument cannot do without
goal: Separate a required assumption from a powerful but optional sufficient bridge.
teaching: A necessary assumption is something the argument needs. It need not prove the conclusion by itself. If the argument concludes that Jo can enter using a ticket rule, it must assume that the rule applies to Jo’s ticket. A rule admitting everyone could guarantee entry but is not required.

Check whether the negation defeats that route, rather than merely weakening it a little.

title: Read some, most and all precisely
goal: Distinguish existence, majority and universal membership.
teaching: Some means at least one. It permits one, several or all. Most means more than half of the stated population. All means every member satisfies the claim, but a universal statement alone does not establish that the population has members.

Keep the reference population fixed. Most musicians read does not say most readers are musicians. Some overlap is reversible: a person who is both a musician and a reader witnesses both statements. No means zero overlap. Many and few have no exact numerical cutoff without context.

Combine a count with a rule one member at a time. Most of six inspectors are licensed gives at least four licensed inspectors.
